title: Immune Effector Cell-associé Neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) Consensus Grading pour adultes
diseases: Syndrome de neurotoxicité associé aux cellules effectrices immunitaires (ICANS)
abbreviations: American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy
formula:
The ICANS Consensus Grading is determined by the most severe event not attributable to any other cause:

| Neurotoxicity Domain | ICANS Grade | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ICE Score](nabda:calc.immune-effector-cell-encephalopathy-ice-score\) ¹ | 10 | Not defined |
| 7-9 | 1 | |
| 3-6 | 2 | |
| 0-2 | 3 | |
| 0 (patient is unarousable and unable to perform ICE) | 4 | |
| Depressed level of consciousness² | Alert | Not defined |
| Awakens spontaneously | 1 | |
| Awakens to voice | 2 | |
| Awakens only to tactile stimulus | 3 | |
| Unarousable or requires vigorous or repetitive tactile stimuli to arouse (stupor or coma) | 4 | |
| Seizure | No seizure | Not defined |
| Any clinical seizure focal or generalized that resolves rapidly or nonconvulsive seizures on EEG that resolve with intervention | 3 | |
| Life-threatening prolonged seizure (> 5 min); or repetitive clinical or electrical seizures without return to baseline in between | 4 | |
| Motor findings³ | No deep focal motor weakness | Not defined |
| Deep focal motor weakness such as hemiparesis or paraparesis | 4 | |
| Elevated ICP /cerebral edema | No evidence of ICP/cerebral edema | Not defined |
| Focal/local edema on neuroimaging⁴ | 3 | |
| Diffuse cerebral edema on neuroimaging; decerebrate or decorticate posturing; or cranial nerve VI palsy; or papilledema; or Cushing's triad | 4 | |
| Death | Not applicable | Not defined |
| Death due to ICANS where another cause is not the principle factor | 5 | |

¹ A patient with an ICE score of 0 may be classified as grade 3 ICANS if awake with global aphasia, but a patient with an ICE score of 0 may be classified as grade 4 ICANS if unarousable.
² Depressed level of consciousness should be attributable to no other cause (eg, no sedating medication).
³ Tremors and myoclonus associated with immune effector cell therapies may be graded according to CTCAE v5.0, but they do not influence ICANS grading.
⁴ Intracranial hemorrhage with or without associated edema is not considered a neurotoxicity feature and is excluded from ICANS grading. It may be graded according to CTCAE v5.0.

how_to_use.why:
- Provides a unified approach for grading ICANS, which can guide management.
- Most recent consensus grading by a national organization.
how_to_use.when:
- Use for adults and adolescents (≥12 years) receiving an immune effector cell engaging therapy to detect and grade immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS); not limited to patients receiving CAR T-cell therapy.
- Use a different grading system for children <12 years old.
- Apply at baseline and serially post-infusion (authors recommend every 8 hours while hospitalized after therapy).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Élaboré par un groupe de consensus soutenu par l'[American Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (ASTCT)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30592986/), afin de contribuer à standardiser l'évaluation de la neurotoxicité, compte tenu de la subjectivité des autres descriptions d'encéphalopathie.
- Approfondit et simplifie les critères CARTOX antérieurs et évite des mesures lourdes et potentiellement imprécises telles que la pression d'ouverture du LCS.
- Élaboré à partir des systèmes de gradation CTCAE v4.03, CTCAE v5.0 et CARTOX CRES.
- Les barrières linguistiques, les troubles cognitifs préexistants, les sédatifs et d'autres comorbidités peuvent fausser l'évaluation.

next_steps.advice:
- Cet outil ne doit pas constituer la seule base de la prise en charge ; utiliser le jugement clinique et une évaluation clinique complète pour guider la prise en charge.
- Réaliser une évaluation neurologique avant l’administration d’une thérapie engageant les cellules effectrices immunitaires, puis quotidiennement par la suite pendant l’hospitalisation.
- Les facteurs non neurologiques (p. ex., sédation, infection, troubles métaboliques) peuvent fausser la notation ; évaluer et traiter les causes alternatives.
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Evaluate for papilledema or other signs of high intracranial pressure (ICP) in Grade 3 or Grade 4 cases, per NCCN guidelines.
- If elevated ICP is excluded, consider diagnostic lumbar puncture to evaluate Grade 3–4 neurotoxicity.
next_steps.management:
Per[NCCN Guidelines for Management of CAR T-Cell-Related Toxicities](https://www.nccn.org/guidelines/guidelines-detail?category=3&id=1547), consider the following approach:

- **Grade 1:**

 - Supportive care.
 - Consider 1 dose of dexamethasone 10 mg IV.
- **Grade 2:**

 - Supportive care.
 - Give 1 dose of dexamethasone 10 mg IV, then reassess.
 - Repeat every 6–12 hours if no improvement.
- **Grade 3:**

 - ICU care.
 - Give dexamethasone 10 mg IV every 6 hours or methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg every 12 hours.
 - Consider adding anakinra 100 mg every 6 hours if not responsive to steroids or if symptoms worsen.
 - Consider repeat CT head or MR brain every 2–3 days for persistent Grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity.
- **Grade 4:**

 - ICU care.
 - Consider mechanical ventilation for airway protection.
 - Administer high-dose steroids.
 - Consider adding anakinra 100 mg every 6 hours if not responsive to steroids.
 - Consider repeat CT head or MR brain every 2–3 days for persistent Grade 3 or higher neurotoxicity.
 - Treat convulsive status epilepticus per institutional guidelines.

evidence: [Pennisi et al. (2020)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7042979/)compared ICANS grading using the ASTCT 2019 consensus grading with other grading schemes. The ASTCT grading classified a higher proportion of cases as Grade 3 than either CTCAE or CARTOX, and a lower proportion as Grade 4 than CARTOX.
